Sarah / Camila —

Attached are two things: 1) integration-snippets.zip (small JS & Go helpers + README), and 2) the mutual-action-plan-novapay.pdf with timing and owners. Quick technical checklist below, then two inlined snippets you can paste.

Minimum integration checklist (actionable):
- Generate an API key from the Redwood console and store it in your secret manager. We support token rotation via our KMS hooks; see step 5 in the MAP.
- Use our SDKs or call the REST endpoint at https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
- Add header X-Client-Id: novapay-integration and X-Request-Id for traceability.
- Implement idempotency for create-style calls: send Idempotency-Key header for retries.
- Retry policy: retry on 429, 502, 503, 504. Use exponential backoff: base 200ms, multiplier 2, max 5 retries; add jitter.
- Timeouts: per-token streaming < 30s connection timeout; overall request timeout 90s for large-batch generation.
- Rate-limit posture: start at 20% of expected production QPS in canary, then 50% for 24h, then 100% after successful runs. Monitor 429 spike counts in Console.
- Logging: capture latency/tokens and X-Request-Id for support escalations.

JS (node) example (in repo; minimal inline):
const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, clientId: 'novapay-integration' });

async function generatePrompt(prompt) {
  try {
    return await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2', prompt, timeout: 90000, retries: { retries: 5, factor: 2 } });
  } catch (err) {
    // handle or surface to Sentry
    throw err;
  }
}

Go example (http client):
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(body)))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("X-Client-Id", "novapay-integration")
req.Header.Set("Idempotency-Key", idempotencyKey)
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 90 * time.Second}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// implement retry loop on 429/5xx with exponential backoff + jitter

Gotchas / endpoint migration notes:
- Auth differences: Redwood uses short-lived tokens by default for Private deployments; Hosted keys are long-lived. If you currently use static keys, plan to add token rotation hooks.
- Header enforcement: we require X-Client-Id and recommend X-Request-Id for tracing — missing headers can make debugging slower.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming responses (server-sent events) behave differently under proxies; ensure your edge preserves chunked responses.

I'll also attach the two files in the thread. Let me know if you want us to run a quick smoke test script during the walkthrough.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Novapay pilot - initial tech ask — recommended config (final)

Sarah —

Answers inline:
1) Retries & idempotency: For payment-adjacent flows we recommend idempotency + server-side checks. Set retries=0 for non-idempotent charge calls. For read/generation calls that are idempotent, use the 5 retries max (config above). Our SDK exposes a "safeRetries" flag you can toggle per-endpoint.

2) Cloudflare & SSE: Set the Cloudflare "Response Buffering" off and increase the proxy timeout to >= 60s. Ensure you pass through chunked transfer-encoding; we include a small smoke script in the zip to verify.

I've enabled a temporary 2x burst for Tue 2026-09-08 10:15-10:45 UTC for your smoke test (requested by Ben). Monica from Implementation will join the call to run the script.

- Ben: confirm temporary burst quota in HubSpot and update MAP — Ben
